anomalies.observed: On the MCU sheet the USB‑C receptacle VBUS pin (J12.A4) carries the global label 'VBUS'. On the Power sheet 'VBUS' is the mux OUTPUT net (U5 pin 1 OUT -> VBUS -> C11/TP1 -> U8 IN/EN), while the mux input IN2 (U5 pin 2) carries the separate label '+5V'. The only other '+5V' object is an isolated power symbol at the top of the MCU sheet that is not tied to the USB connector. Thus the USB 5 V is applied to the mux output / pre‑buck rail and the mux input IN2 has no source.
anomalies.expected: Per the specification the USB VBUS pin must sit on the '+5V' net that feeds U5 IN2, and 'VBUS' must be only the mux output (the unregulated pre‑buck rail). The spec states: 'J12 ... VBUS pins (A4/A9/B4/B9) -> +5V net -> U5 pin 2/2_1 (IN2)' and 'U5 ... IN2 (pin 2) wired to USB +5V/VBUS ... outputs a single OUT onto the VBUS net ... note this net is named VBUS in the netlist but is distinct from the USB +5V net upstream of the mux.'

evidence.quote: MCU sheet (mcu.kicad_sch, page 1/4 & 2/4): J12 USB_C_Receptacle pin A4 wired to global label 'VBUS'
Power sheet (power.kicad_sch, page 4/4): U5 TPS2121RUXR pin 2 IN2 = '+5V'; pin 1 OUT = 'VBUS' (to C11/TP1/U8.IN)
J12 ... VBUS pins (A4/A9/B4/B9) -> +5V net -> U5 pin 2/2_1 (IN2) ... note this net is named VBUS in the netlist but is distinct from the USB +5V net upstream of the mux

anomalies.impact: The TPS2121 power‑mux arbitration is defeated: USB VBUS is hard‑wired to the mux output / pre‑buck rail instead of to IN2. With the 12 V barrel jack present the mux drives ~12 V onto VBUS while the USB port is tied to the same node, causing supply contention and back‑feeding 12 V into the USB host (potential damage and a USB‑spec violation); with USB only, the buck is powered without the mux's current limit / soft‑start. IN2 is left floating.

parsed.summary: The schematic matches the specification on component identities, values, the heater switch, thermocouple SPI bus and buck regulator, but the USB‑C VBUS pin (J12.A4) is placed on the mux‑output 'VBUS' net rather than the '+5V' net that feeds U5 IN2, bypassing/shorting the power mux against the USB supply.
